request: Check this flight: did a control fault occur, when, and where on the aircraft?

result.headline: No attitude-control fault; throttle cut to 0% at t=115 s with channel 2 pinned at 1100 us, cause unknown.
result.explanation: Attitude follows setpoints throughout. The propulsion command (throttle, output ch[2]) drops from 32% to 0% at 115 s and stays there while the aircraft descends. The data does not show why. A battery-related or deliberate cut is possible.

evidence.shows: Throttle command and ch[2] drop together at t=115 s and stay at 1100 us / 0% to the end (t=130 s).
Relative altitude falls from about 51 m to 12 m after the throttle cut, in an unpowered descent. Airspeed is held at 13-20 m/s.

evidence.quote: t=1.1 s Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: A low-voltage warning appears early in the flight. It is the only logged event and could relate to the cut.

checked.check: Attitude tracking: roll and pitch against their setpoints over the whole flight
checked.result: Roll and pitch follow setpoint steps with 1-3 s lag and no divergence or oscillation. This includes large steps at 22 s and 116 s.

checked.check: Output channels for stuck or erratic values
checked.result: ch0 (1500), ch6 (1500) and ch7 (2040) are constant throughout. ch1, ch3, ch4 and ch5 vary normally. ch2 follows throttle and is pinned at 1100 us from 115 s.
ch2 matches the throttle command: higher throttle gives higher output. 0% throttle gives 1100 us, so the output is obeying a zero command.

effects.why: Loss of thrust, not a control-loop failure.

effects.quote: t=116: roll setpoint -41.6, pitch setpoint -20, pitch -9.3
effects.why: Large attitude excursion after the throttle cut. It is tracked correctly, so it follows the cut.

next_action.action: Check battery voltage and flight-mode and failsafe logs around t=115 s
next_action.why: Settles whether the throttle cut was a commanded failsafe or landing, or an upstream command fault.
how: Pull the full-rate flight log around 105-120 s
Check mode changes and failsafe flags at 115 s
Check battery voltage and current across the flight

outcomes.label: Failsafe or mode change at 115 s
outcomes.means: The throttle cut was a commanded response, not a hardware fault.

outcomes.label: No mode change, throttle command dropped
outcomes.means: There is an upstream propulsion or command fault.

unknowns: Reason for the throttle cut at 115 s
Whether ch[2] is the main motor output (inferred only from its correlation with throttle)
Battery voltage trend, which is not in the data

hypotheses.claim: A control-surface or attitude-loop fault caused tracking errors.
hypotheses.because: Attitude follows setpoints throughout, with no divergence or stuck outputs.

hypotheses.claim: Throttle commanded to zero at 115 s, possibly a battery or low-voltage failsafe or a deliberate cut.
hypotheses.because: Throttle and ch[2] drop together and stay at the minimum while altitude falls.

hypotheses.claim: An unintended throttle command fault from the controller or mixer.
hypotheses.because: Cannot be separated from a commanded cut with this data.

events.what: Low voltage battery warning at 1.1 s
events.why: Only logged event; could relate to the later throttle cut.

events.what: Throttle to 0% and ch[2] at 1100 us
events.why: Abrupt, sustained loss of propulsion command.
